thesis_text: Bottom line: Plaid's revealed screen is ownership and pragmatism, demonstrated through real work and honest failure stories, more than pedigree — but the best-documented non-traditional door (the apprenticeship) is evidenced only as of 2021 and must be re-verified before anyone plans around it. Who gets in (sourced numbers only): no hire-population numbers are claimed — school, feeder and major shares are omitted for lack of a public sample. The only sourced numbers are a single official posting's salary range for one Staff AI role ($264,660-$369,800/yr) and a 90-minute final technical assessment in the 2021 apprentice account. Stated vs revealed screens: Plaid states a mission of financial access and encourages non-perfect-match applications; its engineering leadership reveals screens for overdeveloped responsibility, pragmatism under constraints, and the ability to discuss a real failure reflectively. Ranked entry routes: (1) direct application to an open SWE posting, (2) engineering apprenticeship IF currently running (unverified for 2026), (3) intern/new-grad postings (windows not documented in this pass). Timeline/dates (as of 2026-10-12): no current application windows are sourced; the apprenticeship account is date-stamped 2021-08-20 and is stale. Risks/alternatives: planning around a possibly-paused program is the main risk; API-platform and fintech-infrastructure peers are adjacent hedges. Gap analysis vs a specific user is not computed here (no population sample).
known_biases_of_data: Survivorship bias: the apprentice blog post is a success story published by the employer; it cannot show apprentice acceptance rates or failure modes.
Single-story risk: one documented path is evidence a route exists, not that it is common.
Leadership-interview statements are one executive's described preferences, not audited hiring data.
Glassdoor-style reports are self-selected and unverified; used only as labeled anecdotes.
No H-1B LCA, university-outcome or licensed population data was fetched in this pass.
